title: Close open PRs whose commits land via another merged Athena PR
summary: Record a base job on a job stacked on an unmerged job, and after any Athena PR merges, close each other open Athena PR whose commits are all in main, commenting the merged PR number and marking its job superseded. Audience: the Athena operator, who currently cleans up stacked PRs by hand.

defaults_applied.how: Add unit tests in pr.rs/reconcile.rs; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Tests run the merge-of-B scenario end to end with fakes and assert the close, comment and job state.
One focused change: base-job record plus post-merge sweep.
Verifier runs cargo test on the scenario tests.
Criteria check A's PR closed and job superseded, not that the sweep function exists.
A test requires the sweep to find at least one candidate and also shows an unmerged PR stays open.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Superseded' is a new terminal OutcomeState in athena-data records.rs (existing states: Landed, Rejected, Dropped, Abandoned, ...) and a Closed(...) JobState; adding it must not break reading old records.
The base job is stored in the job's PR link or intent state under the state dir (pr.rs), not in records/.
The sweep hooks the existing merge observation (pr::observe_merge / reconcile) and uses the host trait to close PRs and comment, faked in tests.
'All commits in main' means every PR head commit is an ancestor of main, or its patch is in main via the stacked merge, checked by git ancestry.
Merge-method caveat: squash merges would not make A's commits ancestors of main; I assume only merges that preserve commits count, and a squashed stack is left open.
The sweep is idempotent: an already closed PR or superseded job is skipped.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a new test with job B stacked on unmerged job A, then B's PR merged, shows A's PR closed with a comment naming B's PR number and A's job state superseded, with no other call.
Run cargo test: a new test shows an open Athena PR with at least one commit not in main stays open, its job is unchanged, and it gets no comment after another PR merges.
Run cargo test: a test shows the base job is recorded when a job is started on an unmerged job's branch and is read back.
Run cargo test: running the sweep twice does not post a second comment or change the superseded job.
Superseded appears in job status display and old records without it still parse; cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean.

out_of_scope: Handling squash-merged stacks by patch-id matching
Rewriting or retargeting the merged PR's base
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance: it adds a new outcome state across several crates and needs fake-host tests.
hard_reason: It adds a terminal job outcome state and automatic closing of PRs, which touches records and landing behavior.
